verification: limactl shell local-dev -- sh -c 'cd ~/openlore && cargo test -p adapter-s3-index-object --test scale_to_zero_write_probe'

facts.F1: Trim whitespace before comparing index_key and last_pass_key against WRITE_PROBE_KEY in location_names_write_probe_key (crates/ports/src/probe.rs) so padded marker keys are refused at init and connect (scale-to-zero-hosting LOW: marker-key trim).
facts.F10: An oracle that tests only untrimmed equality or ASCII spaces on a single key does not see whether both index_key and last_pass_key are trimmed identically or whether non-space whitespace (such as tabs or newlines) is handled consistently.
facts.F11: When neither index_key nor last_pass_key trims to WRITE_PROBE_KEY (including empty or whitespace-only keys, keys with extra non-whitespace characters, path-prefixed/suffixed keys, or keys with internal whitespace), location_names_write_probe_key returns false.
facts.F12: An oracle that checks only a single ordinary unrelated key does not see false positives on near-miss keys containing WRITE_PROBE_KEY as a substring, prefix, suffix, or case variant, nor on whitespace-only keys.
facts.F13: S3IndexObjectAdapter::connect refuses with an error any location whose index_key or last_pass_key equals WRITE_PROBE_KEY directly or after trimming leading or trailing whitespace.
facts.F14: An oracle that checks only exact untrimmed keys or only index_key does not see whether last_pass_key with surrounding whitespace is also refused, whether refusal occurs before any remote S3 network call or storage mutation, or whether the error distinguishes key refusal from unrelated connection failures.
facts.F15: S3IndexObjectAdapter::connect does not reject a location on the write-probe-key guard when neither index_key nor last_pass_key trims to WRITE_PROBE_KEY.
facts.F16: An oracle that only asserts connect returns an error for probe keys does not distinguish targeted probe-key refusal from a blanket connection failure or overly broad substring matching.
facts.F2: Prevent whitespace-padded index or last-pass keys from bypassing the write-probe marker key refusal
facts.F20: An implementation that trims only ASCII whitespace (space, tab, carriage return, newline) rather than non-ASCII Unicode whitespace would still pass
facts.F21: Connect to an object-store location whose index key or pass-record key has leading or trailing whitespace around the write-probe marker, and connect to locations with non-marker keys
facts.F22: Refuses connection with a probe refusal error when either key trims to the write-probe marker and succeeds for non-marker locations
facts.F23: Startup refuses any configured store location whose index or pass-record key trims to the write-probe marker and accepts valid non-marker locations
facts.F24: An implementation that trims only ASCII whitespace when checking keys at connect time rather than non-ASCII Unicode whitespace would still pass
facts.F25: Check whether an index key, pass-record key, or both with leading or trailing spaces, tabs, or newlines around the write-probe marker are recognized as the marker, and whether empty, whitespace-only, uppercase case-variant, padded non-marker, prefixed or suffixed marker paths, and keys with internal whitespace are allowed
facts.F26: Returns true whenever either or both keys trim to the write-probe marker and false for empty, whitespace-only, case-variant, and all other non-marker keys
facts.F27: Any index or pass-record key (or both) whose trimmed text matches the write-probe marker is identified as the marker, while empty, whitespace-only, case-variant, and distinct keys are permitted
